This is the adopted workflow's authority for SD stages and task schema. Resolve
its absolute directory and retain `--workflow-dir` on SD commands, including
worker reads and recovery. Skills guide work; SD owns dispatch, gates and state.

## File Naming

Each task is a flat `<slug>.md` file in the resolved state checkout. Keep existing
IDs and tasks in their recorded workflow; new work does not migrate old work.

## Schema

Record `id`, `title`, `status`, `variant: kc-dev-flow-2`, and the user's selected
`profile`. The five-stage route accepts `pilot` or `prod`; the POC adaptation
removes ideation from both frontmatter and Stages and accepts `poc` only.
Before admission and dispatch, FO checks that the selected profile matches this
workflow's actual ordered stages. Unknown/mismatched profiles require a hold,
not an invented transition or default. SD does not enforce this profile rule.
Preserve the approved outcome, scope, non-goals, budget and stop condition in the
body. Use bold **AC-N** declarations with individual evidence clauses.

## Stages

Stage workers run on the workflow's default model.
`kc-dev-flow-2:chief-engineer`, `kc-dev-flow-2:engineering-reviewer` and
`kc-dev-flow-2:observer` run on the model and reasoning their agent files declare, never
a cheaper one. Record chief-engineer and engineering-reviewer calls under `## FO alignment` as
`Reviewer: <agent> <model> <date> — <question>`; `<package>/scripts/role_triggers.py` lists calls owed.

`concurrency` limits only what `status --next` proposes. A feedback-reflow repair and an
FO fix authorized under Review-finding disposition step 3 are dispatched at once in the
entity's own worktree, after the existing overlap check against running worktrees; they
do not wait for another entity's worker in the same stage. The validation recheck of
that repair or fix does not wait for another entity's worker either, but it is
dispatched only after the repair or fix has completed and committed its candidate, so
the validator reads the bytes that will be delivered. A repair that outgrows what its
assignment names returns to FO as a scope change.

FO resolves `<package>` in this workflow from the `Package root:` line of
`kc-dev-flow-2:dev`. Before each worker dispatch FO runs `python3 <package>/scripts/package_version.py
<this README>`; exit 1 means the session loaded an older package than this README was synced
from, and FO holds the dispatch until the session runs the newer one. FO also runs
`python3 <package>/scripts/workflow_checkout.py <this README>`, which compares this file with
`origin/<trunk>`'s: exit 1 means they differ, exit 2 that it could not compare, and FO
holds the dispatch and shows the Captain what the script printed. Every worker dispatch FO builds carries that absolute path as a
`Package root: <absolute path>` line in its scope notes (`--scope-notes-file`), which
land in the dispatch file the worker reads first. Those scope notes, and every follow-up
message to a live worker, also carry ``Send your completion message to `main` (the README's Dispatch
facts: `team-lead` is not registered here).``: the builder's completion block names `team-lead`, and a
worker that skips the stage-definition fetch does not see the Signal fact. FO saves those scope notes, the
checklist, the model it dispatches on and the SHA it dispatches from as
`<task>/dispatch/<stage>-<cycle>.md` in the state checkout (for validation a
`Candidate: <full head SHA>` line per head validated),
committed with that dispatch's `spacedock state commit <slug> --workflow-dir <dir>`, so

`python3 <package>/scripts/dispatch_records.py <task folder>` before committing and fixes each part it lists. A follow-up
message to a worker FO resumes is a dispatch too, with the same check and a checklist of the items that message asks, never a pointer to another record.
A checklist or scope-notes line that names a package script writes
`<package>/scripts/NAME.py` with the absolute root substituted, never the bare script

on the saved record and rewrites each name it lists. When `status --set` refuses to leave a stage, run `spacedock status --workflow-dir
<dir> --read <task> --stage <stage> --checklist`, return any line it reports as neither
DONE nor SKIPPED to the worker, and do not edit the worker's report. The refusal itself

### `backlog`

The user selects the compatible profile and approves outcome, scope and budget.
FO records the choice; this boundary has no worker or placeholder report. FO
also records, under a `## FO alignment` heading in the task file, whether FO
direction alignment with the Captain is needed before the next declared stage
and why; a
stated reason is the whole record when not needed. On the five-stage route, FO
also records a `Surfaces:` line under the same heading: any of `ui`, `db`,
or `none`, read from the change surface rather than the diff, and next to it
a `Visible change:` line: one sentence on what a user sees or operates
differently, or `Visible change: none`.

- **Gate content:** Show the selected variant/profile, proposed outcome, scope,
  exclusions and evidence needed before the next declared stage starts, the
  `## FO alignment` need and reason, and the recorded `Surfaces:` and
  `Visible change:` lines on the five-stage route.
- **Seed check:** On the five-stage route, before `gate prepare`, FO runs
  `python3 <package>/scripts/design_surfaces.py check --seed <task>` and holds the
  gate until it exits 0. An FO that skips this step still dispatches; the worker's own
  check is the backstop.
- **Release review:** Applies to a task that belongs to a release on a journey map
  (`journey`, `journey-release`, `journey-story`); a task with no release, such as a
  bug, infrastructure or workflow maintenance, is outside it. Four signals: (1) a task
  admitted into a release; (2) a Captain scope ruling that moves a story or task into
  or out of a release or changes the goal of the release, a story or a task; (3) a UAT
  failure that crosses two or more tasks; (4) a batch about to enter implementation. Signals 1 and 2 only mark the
  release changed: FO names the release and the signal in the task's `## FO alignment`
  reason. A task whose `journey-story` is already on the map in that release passes with
  that one check and marks nothing when, since its latest `Release review:` line, the
  journey file still holds the same story ids and the same release and story `goal`
  text and no Captain ruling has changed the goal of the release, a story or a task.
  A changed goal is signal 2 although no story id moved; FO marks the release
  changed in that task's `## FO alignment` reason. Signal 4 is the single checkpoint: at the first
  implementation dispatch for a release marked changed, FO dispatches a fresh worker
  with kc-journey-map's `review-release` mode, then splits tasks from its output; an
  unchanged release proceeds. One review covers every change since the last. Signal 3
  runs the review at once. FO writes no map and no candidate; the Captain accepts
  membership in conversation or at this gate. FO records under `## FO alignment` either
  `Release review: <journey>/<release-id> at <journey-file commit>` or
  `Release review: not needed: <reason>`; no script checks that line. When FO approves
  a task into a release story at this gate it sets the three fields with
  `spacedock status --workflow-dir <dir> --set <task> journey=<the map's journey: value> journey-release=<id> journey-story=<id>`;
  a worker never edits frontmatter. Where the adopter tracks completion with
  kc-journey-progress, FO also writes `journey-required-tasks` (full task ids) and
  `journey-mapping-complete: true` on one task per story at the review's split step.
  When signal 2 moves a task out of a release, FO clears its release fields with
  `spacedock status --workflow-dir <dir> --set <task> journey= journey-release= journey-story= journey-required-tasks= journey-mapping-complete=`
  (a field set to nothing is cleared). Where kc-journey-progress is tracking, follow its
  skill for the lists; when the cleared task was the declaring one, FO moves that list and
  `journey-mapping-complete: true` to another member of the story. kc-journey-progress
  reports a story unverified until its declaration matches its members.

## Review-finding disposition

Before repair authorization, product bytes and the recorded candidate revision stay
unchanged. Read-only inspection, non-mutating reproductions, existing tests and
throwaway-checkout probes are allowed. Report/gate commits may advance repository
HEAD without changing the candidate. Validators recommend `PASSED` or `REJECTED`;
new findings or changed evidence re-enter this checkpoint.

The four evidence fields are released user and normal workflow; observable harm;
affected value acceptance criterion or non-negotiable boundary; and trigger
evidence. Field 3 uses `value-ac[AC-N]`, `captain-ruling[YYYY-MM-DD]`, or
`contract[repo/relative/path#anchor]` plus a nonblank claim. `none:` with a rationale
does not establish Material.

- **Material:** all four fields establish supported-workflow harm to a protected
  boundary or value acceptance criterion.
- **Deferred risk:** hypothetical, unsupported, unobserved or unpromised trigger;
  record what would make it material.
- **Polish:** no current user-visible loss or protected boundary is at risk.
- **Needs decision:** the task cannot own the scope, product or compatibility call.

A `Follow-up:` line in Scope is not accepted scope by itself: the first stage of the
receiving task to meet it assesses it against its stated reason and earlier rulings. It builds the line only when the change alters no behaviour that an
accepted criterion, a Captain ruling or a journey contract relies on; otherwise it
returns the line to FO as a Needs decision. It records which, and why.
A finding FO declined in a committed gate summary or under `### FO declines` is settled:
a later validator does not report it again unless the candidate changes the lines or the
evidence the decline names, or new evidence would make it Material.

## FO steps: review findings

Apply this checkpoint to findings from implementation, validation, detached audits,
consequential FO quick work and rejected gates.

1. Reviewers observe; workers' classifications and `actor:ensign` Resolutions are
   advisory. Preserve findings and assess the four evidence fields above, separating
   materiality, ownership and disposition. Missing required evidence or unresolved
   classification requires investigation or hold.
2. Within approved boundaries, FO may explicitly decline evidenced Deferred risk or
   Polish in the existing committed gate summary, naming the finding, reason, candidate
   revision and the lines or evidence it rests on. When that summary is already
   consumed, FO writes the decline under `### FO declines` in the task file, committed
   with `spacedock state commit <slug> --workflow-dir <dir>`, and the terminal gate
   lists each entry there. This FO-authored decision requires no live worker or reviewer
   rerun for acknowledgement; preserve worker reports and verdicts.
3. Repairs require worker investigation without candidate mutation, distinct FO
   `fix` authorization through the runtime's addressable-worker boundary, then
   independent validation. Without that authorization, hold.
4. Scope, value, threshold, tolerance, risk-acceptance and acceptance-criteria
   changes require the Captain. Material findings cannot use the record-only lane;
   hold/route-for-decision forbids repair and reviewer rerun.
5. A round is one verdict of an external reviewer of the delivery on the PR head (Codex
   on the PR, RoboRev or another); FO counts rounds and records the count in the
   committed gate summary. A reviewer that a listed extension covers is read the way its
   `EXTENSION.md` says (`## Extensions`). A finding assessed Material, or labelled P1 by
   the reviewer, blocks in every round: a reviewer P1 is fixed and revalidated, or
   waived by the Captain with the reason recorded (step 4). For an external reviewer
   that has no P1 label, its highest severity level counts as P1 (e.g. RoboRev). Rounds
   1 and 2 follow steps 1 to 4. From round 3 a finding that is neither does not start a
   repair cycle: FO declines it in the committed gate summary, naming the finding, and
   files it as a new backlog task with `spacedock new` whose body carries the finding
   and the decline reason, or names the backlog task that already holds it when a later
   round repeats it; it never enters an open task's Scope. The terminal gate lists each
   such task.

Rejection routing carries evidence, classifications, authorized dispositions and assignment
without re-triage.

Materiality and ownership are independent. Owned Material is eligible for an
FO-authorized fix; out-of-scope Material holds as Needs decision. Deferred risk
or Polish may use the recorded FO decline above within existing risk acceptance.

A Needs decision put to the Captain at a gate carries FO's recommendation. His
plain approval accepts that recommendation only when the gate question says so,
for example "approving accepts the recommendation for D2; say if you object".
Without that sentence a decision he did not address stays open: FO records its
handling as FO's reading, never as his ruling, and asks him.

A decision an accepted ADR already settles is not asked again: FO applies it and states it
in the gate summary as `Precedent: ADR <number> — 「<that ADR's Words line>」`, and the
Captain may reopen it. An ADR with no Words line is quoted by the decision sentence it
applies, as `Precedent: ADR <number> (no Words line) — 「<that sentence>」`. Authority, a gate approval, a merge, an outward-facing action, an
irreversible change and money are always asked, whatever an ADR says, and an ADR on one
of them is never a `Precedent:` line.

A Captain ruling is his reply to the question it settles, given after that question
was put. FO never records as his ruling: silence on a decision the question did not
state approval accepts, consent he gave earlier to a different question, or a choice
he raised but did not make. FO answers a question the Captain asks at a gate before
dispatching on it, and returns a choice he raised to him rather than to a worker.

When the Captain chooses differently from the recommendation, FO writes
`Override: recommended <option>; Captain chose <option>; area: <area>` in the gate
resolution reason, so later workers find past rulings with `git grep 'Override:'` in
the state checkout.

## Decision records

The implementation worker writes one ADR file per decision by its stage principles.
Validation runs `python3 <package>/scripts/adr_lint.py docs/adr --since <base>`, which
requires every record the candidate added or changed, plus `--require <numbers>` for
each `ADR:` number the task's `## Number guards` reserves and any number the
implementation report names; exit 1 or a missing record returns through the existing
feedback route, and exit 2 is a configuration error that returns to FO.

## FO steps: decision records

A ruling settled at a gate, in a worker report, or mid-stage feedback — a rule about
the product, a constraint, or a direction later work must respect — is landed as an
ADR before the next gate is presented, at latest by the terminal approval. A ruling
that governs only this task's own work stays in the task. A design names an ADR
by its ruling and the file's short title, with no number; FO reserves the number when
it dispatches implementation (Number guards) and the implementation worker writes
`docs/adr/<reserved number>-<short-title>.md`. FO confirms the validation ADR lint
passes before presenting the gate. A deferred user-facing capability belongs on
the product's journey map, not here.

## Captain amendments

A change the Captain makes to what he has accepted, whether at a gate approval,
during implementation or at a validation gate, is an amendment. A change he asks for
while the gate that would accept it is still open is not one: he calls `revise`; at a stage
with no `feedback-to` that dispatches a worker, that stage's worker reworks it; at a stage
whose gate has a `feedback-to`, the revision goes to that target and the stage's worker
re-reviews it; and at `backlog`, which dispatches no worker, FO revises the recorded outcome,
scope or budget, or asks the proposal's author to.

FO appends one entry per amendment to the task's `## Captain amendments` section and
changes nothing else in it. FO adds no words of its own and does not move or rewrite a criterion:

```
## Captain amendments

### Amendment 1 — <date>, <gate or chat>
Captain: 「<his words, verbatim>」 (where he said them)
Asked: <the question or proposal he answered, verbatim, or the commit holding it>
Supersedes: <acceptance-criterion ids, or none> <optional: "(no replacement: <why>)">
Design: <optional: the design paragraph it overrides>
```

`Asked:` is required when his words do not name what they settle, such as 「同意第三點」. FO
names the amendment in the next dispatch's checklist. That worker (implementation, the
repair worker on a feedback route, or the worker of the stage a task is sent back to)
moves each superseded criterion's block verbatim from `## Acceptance criteria` into its
entry under a `Superseded text:` line, writes any replacement as a new `**AC-N**` under
a fresh id that says "Amended by Captain, amendment N", and never reuses an id. A
superseded criterion and the design paragraph named by `Design:` are withdrawn; evidence
and the Captain's acceptance script follow `## Acceptance criteria` plus the entries.

Sending an approved task back to an earlier stage, such as a design redo a release
review asks for, is the Captain's decision and is recorded as an amendment whose
`Design:` names what is redone; FO then runs `spacedock status --workflow-dir <dir>
--set <slug> status=<stage>`, and that stage's gate is approved again before the task
moves on.

`python3 <package>/scripts/design_surfaces.py check <task>`, run by implementation and
validation, prints each defect and exits 1; repair findings return through feedback. It cannot see a skipped record or
move, or FO's words in `Design:`.

## Number guards

Applies when the task's `Surfaces:` includes `db`, or the task lands an ADR, including one first required by a ruling in a worker report or mid-stage feedback, whose number FO reserves before the next dispatch; the POC bullet below applies to every `poc` task.
`python3 <package>/scripts/number_guards.py --help` lists the flags and rules R1 to R6;
`trunk:`, `migrations-path:` and `adr-path:` (default `docs/adr`) come from this README's frontmatter.

- **Applied.** `check` freezes a migration in a commit recorded `Applied at:` (R2).
  `Applied: none as of <sha>` records that
  nothing was pushed up to that commit; a validator that finds none of `Applied at:`,
  `Not applied:` or `Applied: none` reports the missing record to FO instead of
  re-checking deploys. A task with no `Migration:` line owes none of these.
- **Check.** `python3 <package>/scripts/number_guards.py check --workflow-dir <workflow-dir> --task <task file>`
  runs at implementation exit, at validation and, after `git -C <repo> fetch`, on the PR
  head before FO asks for merge. Exit 2 is a configuration error, which returns to FO
  as a hold.
- **POC.** A task whose recorded `profile` is `poc` adds, edits and deletes no migration
  file and reserves no number. A `FAIL R6` crosses the POC boundary
  (a schema change persists across sessions): the worker records
  `boundary-crossed: persistent-state` naming the path, and the task is not repaired in
  place.

## FO steps: number guards

- **Reserve.** Before an implementation dispatch, FO runs `git -C <repo> fetch`, then
  `python3 <package>/scripts/number_guards.py reserve --kind migration|adr --workflow-dir <workflow-dir> --repo <repo> --task <task file>`
  once per kind the task needs, when the implementation dispatch is built and not
  earlier; a task holds one number per kind, and a task needing a second ADR or
  migration returns to FO. FO records each printed `Migration: NNNN` /
  `ADR: NNNN` line under `## Number guards` in the task and repeats the lines as
  dispatch scope notes.
- **Applied.** Before any push of a candidate to a persistent shared non-production
  environment (a database branch, or a separate hosting project such as a staging
  project whose database is that project's own production database), FO records `Applied at: <environment> <sha>`
  for the commit being pushed. When the push is rejected or the
  deploy is confirmed not to have run for that commit (the push's non-zero output,
  or the environment's own deploy record showing no deploy of it), FO replaces that
  one line with `Not applied: <environment> <sha> - <evidence>` and the migration is
  no longer frozen. Without that confirmation the line stays and the migration counts
  as applied. When FO dispatches validation and nothing was pushed for the task, FO
  records `Applied: none as of <candidate sha>`, so a task with neither line has a
  skipped record. A task with no `Migration:` line records no `Applied:` line.
- **POC marker.** FO presents the `boundary-crossed: persistent-state` marker at the
  validation gate. Without `migrations-path:` the migration rules are skipped, so a POC
  is not guarded until the README declares it.
- **Collision.** When two tasks hold one migration number (`check` reports R3 or R5 on
  the later candidate; nothing compares task files), the task whose migration is applied
  keeps it and the other, unapplied task renumbers, so no reset is needed. A migration
  counts as applied when its task has an `Applied at:` line or it is on the base branch;
  when both tasks are applied and neither is on the base branch, the one that merges
  first keeps the number. The renumbering task deletes its `Migration:` line, FO runs
  `reserve` again, and the task returns to implementation with the new number in its
  scope notes. When the renumbering task has an `Applied at:` line, its environment's
  database holds a migration no branch will carry, and FO holds for the Captain: a
  database branch is reset, and a shared non-production database that cannot be reset
  (a separate project's own database) is deleted and recreated by the Captain. FO then
  replaces the line with `Not applied: <environment> <sha> - database reset` so that
  `check` accepts the renumber. A branch database is reset through the provider's own API; `adoption.md` gives one
  provider's example. This step is documented, not wrapped in a tool.

## Delivery authority

The adopted `_mods/pr-merge.md` is the unmodified mod from the activated SD
package. Before delivery, confirm the file still matches the reviewed source
(or an explicitly approved project customization) and its merge hook is
registered. Missing/changed delivery configuration requires a hold: `merge: pr`
alone does not block SD's no-hook local-finalize route.

Project and Captain authority constrain hook instructions: present the exact candidate and
PR body before authorized push/create; create a Draft PR where required, and request ready
only after the required CI is green. Where CI skips drafts, FO marks the PR ready under
the Captain's authority and waits for those jobs before asking for merge. Approval of a
validation gate is not permission to push, create or merge a PR, except as follows. FO's
delivery gate question says approval also covers later external-review rounds on the same
PR, merging the full head `<package>/scripts/delivery_gate.py check` passes, with
`--match-head-commit` set to it, unless he says he merges or holds, and removing its
clean, pushed worktree. Under that approval, a repair whose validation passes with no
Material or Needs decision finding is recorded by FO
(`gate record --actor agent:first-officer` with `--conn-quote` and `--conn-source` naming
his approval) and pushed to that PR's branch, after confirming the pushed commit is the
candidate the report names. A rejected repair, a Needs decision and a scope change go to
him. Preserve manual merge authority. Do not invoke local fallback, push the trunk, merge,
or clean up an owned worktree unless the specific action is authorized. An upstream hook's
default fallback is not that grant. A failure holds delivery pending an explicit choice.

Under the Captain's grant quoted in its dispatch, the implementation worker opens the task's
Draft PR before validation; that grant stands in for a presented body. Observe the actual
repository-qualified PR merge before recording its landed sentinel and running SD merge guard
to finalize/archive. Where `learn` is listed, the sentinel waits for a committed observer report.
CI green, PR creation, gate approval and a locally manufactured sentinel do not prove merge.
FO's startup and idle steps are in `_mods/kc-dev-flow-2.md`, copied from `<package>/references/sd/mods/`.

Before merging or asking, FO runs `python3 <package>/scripts/delivery_gate.py check <task>
--pr <owner/repo>#<N> --text-file <question and summary>`; exit 1 or 2 holds the ask, as does a head other than the latest `Candidate:`; FO shows the Captain what it printed.

`merge guard --rework` supersedes the approval and routes the task back, but its
help names no commit or publish step, unlike the archive path. After it, FO runs
`spacedock state commit <slug> --workflow-dir <dir>`, publishes, and reads the task
back from the state remote before dispatching the repair; otherwise durable state
can still show the task awaiting merge.

## Extensions

Extensions are optional accessories in `<package>/extensions/<name>/`, each described by
its `EXTENSION.md`: what it needs, the stage or FO step it joins, the instruction it
adds, how its result is read, and what happens when it cannot run. This README's
frontmatter `extensions:` lists the ones this repository uses; an unlisted extension is
not probed and adds nothing. For a listed extension FO follows its `EXTENSION.md`: at a
worker dispatch of its stage FO adds its instruction line to the scope notes, and at its
FO step FO reads the result as the file says. A listed extension that cannot run, or that FO does not request because a ruling says not to, is
reported as `<name> not run: <reason>` in the stage report or gate summary, and never
counts as a clean result. A merge ask names each listed reviewer that was not read, and
the Captain decides. Where two remote reviewers are listed, frontmatter `second-reviewer:`
names the one that joins only when a trigger holds: the task's `Surfaces:` include `db`,
its profile is `prod`, a dispatch said its design is hard to reverse, the change touches authority,
approval, merge or review rules, or the Captain asks. FO records `second reviewer: <name>
because <trigger>` or `second reviewer: not triggered` in the gate summary, and an
untriggered second reviewer is not named as unread.

The README and `_mods` stay in the code repository; mutable task state lives in

# 0016. The amendment check refuses an unnamed move and an unmarked replacement

Date: 2026-10-16

## Status

Accepted

## Context

ADR 0005 made `design_surfaces.py check` refuse an amendment entry with no `Captain:` line and a superseded id still declared. The observer reports on archived tasks `delivery-gate-verdict-form` and `fo-lifecycle-mod` found FO-written amendments that broke the README `## Captain amendments` form while `check` printed `design surfaces presentable` (run 2026-10-16 on the committed archive copies, exit 0 each): six replacement criteria without "Amended by Captain, amendment N", and an entry whose `Supersedes:` line read `none` while seven criteria sat in it. Read-only run over 43 task files with amendment entries in this workflow, relay, qnow and subspace-web (2026-10-16): 74 entries, and the two new rules refuse 10 errors on 8 tasks. Read one by one, 7 errors on 6 tasks break the README form (unmarked or variant-phrased replacements, an unnamed move, a move recorded outside its entry); 1 (`owner-sees-all-feedback-room` amendment 3) moved criteria to a new task and clears with the waiver below; 2 (`staff-multi-branch` amendment 1) moved criteria to a new task, which the waiver covers, and also moved clauses of criteria that stay declared, which no waiver covers.

## Decision

**Words:** 「准」 — Captain, 2026-10-16, at the ideation gate of `amendment-form-check`; the gate question stated that approval accepts each decision as recommended. Decision D1 as recommended: refuse a replacement with no marking phrase, with a waiver written on the `Supersedes:` line.

**Options considered:**
- `check` also refuses an entry holding a criterion its `Supersedes:` line does not name, and an entry that supersedes ids when no criterion says "Amended by Captain, amendment N" and the line lacks "no replacement" (chosen)
- refuse only the moved criterion the line does not name — not chosen: the unmarked replacement then stays visible only to the observer, after the PR
- also scan `Design:` for FO's own words — not chosen: 34 of 35 non-`none` values in the corpus are FO prose the form allows, so no text rule separates a pointer from a paraphrase

**Recommended:** the first option, as the Captain accepted.

The rule later work must follow: `check` exits 1 for a criterion held in an entry that `Supersedes:` does not name, and for an entry whose `Supersedes:` names ids when no criterion declaration line (one starting `**AC-N**`) in `## Acceptance criteria` or in another entry's moved text carries "Amended by Captain, amendment N" for its number, unless the line says "no replacement". It supplements ADR 0005 and leaves its decision standing.

## Consequences

FO writes one more token on the `Supersedes:` template. A worker can type "no replacement" falsely, and one marked criterion satisfies an entry whose other replacements are unmarked. `check` still cannot see a skipped move or FO's words in `Design:`; the observer keeps both. A partial move of a criterion's clause (corpus: `staff-multi-branch` amendment 1) is refused: the form has no partial move, and naming the id fails the still-declared rule. Only a line starting `**AC-N**` is read as a criterion, so evidence prose neither moves a criterion nor marks a replacement; evidence on the same line as a declaration can still carry the marker, and a marker written only on a `Replaced by:` line is refused. Entries already archived with these breaks now fail `check`; a runner that executes `check` over closed tasks would report them. Reopen if a task needs a partial supersession.

# 0003. The package documents secret-read enforcement and ships no hook

Date: 2026-09-30

## Status

Accepted

## Context

Two workers in an adopting project printed a development secret key despite dispatch
notes banning it. A user-level `PreToolUse` Bash guard has held since, but its
patterns match the whole command text, so it also refused a read-only command that
only mentioned a guarded tool name as test data. A plugin `hooks/hooks.json`
`PreToolUse` hook was probed on Claude Code 2.1.284 and fired in an unrelated
project's working directory, so a shipped hook would fire wherever the package is
enabled, including repositories with no dev2 adoption and machines that already
carry the user's own guard. The patterns depend on the adopter's stack, and Codex
has no `PreToolUse` equivalent. Read 2026-09-30 in the task's ideation.
A real worker, given a checklist item that named `comment_ratio.py` with no root,
searched the whole filesystem for it in its first batched command, before it had
read the section or loaded a skill (validation cycle 2).

## Decision

**Words:** 「准」 — Captain, 2026-09-30, at the ideation gate of `dispatch-and-report-hygiene` (document the secret guard, do not ship it)

**Words, package-root correction:** 「准」 — Captain, 2026-09-30, on validation cycle 2 of `dispatch-and-report-hygiene` (the first officer states the package root in every dispatch)

**Options considered:**
- document the guard contract in `references/sd/adoption.md` and name one run-time wrapper in the dispatch's `Secrets:` line, shipping no hook
- ship a `hooks/hooks.json` `PreToolUse` entry in the package — rejected: it fires in every project where the plugin is enabled, doubles the user-level guard, cannot carry per-adopter patterns, and is Claude-only
- list the forbidden commands in each dispatch — rejected: two leaks happened despite such bans

The package does not ship a secret-read hook. Secret-read enforcement belongs to the
adopter or the user; the package states the contract in `references/sd/adoption.md`
and the workflow's `## Dispatch facts` names one wrapper as the only route to a
development secret. Facts only the package knows are stated by its skills (the
`Package root:` line and the FAILED rule); facts about the runtime and the adopter
are stated by that one inlined section. A worker composes its first commands from
the dispatch file before it loads a skill or reads that section, so the first
officer also writes the skill's `Package root:` value into the scope notes of every
worker dispatch and writes every package script it names as `<package>/scripts/NAME`
with that root substituted.

## Consequences

An adopter that never reads `adoption.md` and installs no guard stays protected only
by the `Secrets:` line, which failed twice. A worker that splits or encodes a command
to pass a guard is forbidden by the sentence and detected by nothing. Reopen if a leak
is observed in an adopter that followed the contract, or if Codex gains a pre-tool
hook the package could target.

`<package>` is the `Package root:` line of `kc-dev-flow-2:dev`.

## Hook: startup

1. Run the idle hook below.

## Hook: idle

1. Run `python3 <package>/scripts/pr_watch.py tasks <workflow dir>`.
2. Do each `next:` line it prints, in order.
3. After the `pr-merge` hook, do each `after pr-merge:` line it printed.

# 0011. FO decides for the Captain only by a four-level delegation ladder

Date: 2026-10-12

## Status

Accepted

## Context

The Captain wants dev2 to learn his decision trajectory and, at high confidence, decide
on his behalf: 「讓 FO 可以依據 ADR 以及自我學習與改進的結果，可以代替我決策」 (chat,
2026-10-12). ADR 0009 covers the same direction for package self-improvement only, and
left open how work is triggered when a task closes.

Two facts measured on 2026-10-12 over one adopter's state branch (its active and archived task files)
bear on it. `python3 kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/decision_ledger.py` read 168 gate resolutions and
15 withdrawals, matching `grep -c` of `decision:`, `resolution:` and `withdrawal:` lines;
9 resolutions were recorded by `agent:first-officer` under a quoted grant. No gate record
carries an `Override:` line, so no area yet shows when the Captain chose against FO.

## Decision

**Words:** 「可以，就照此方向。」 — Captain, chat, 2026-10-12

**Asked:** 「**要你決定：** 照這個方向做下一批嗎？內容是 learn 擴充（歸檔時觸發）加上決策帳本，再加 L2「依先例代決」。L3 等資料夠了再說。我建議做，並把整條授權階梯另外寫成一份 ADR，和 ADR 0009 互相引用。」

**Options considered:**
- a four-level ladder, built up from L2, with L3 waiting for ledger data (chosen)
- not in this batch, the other answer to the yes-or-no question asked

**Recommended:** the four-level ladder

FO decides for the Captain only at one of four levels:

- **L0:** FO recommends; the Captain decides. The default.
- **L1:** a gate question that says approval accepts FO's recommendation (workflow
  README, `## FO steps: review findings`).
- **L2, decide by precedent:** a decision an accepted ADR already settles is applied by
  FO and stated in the gate summary as `Precedent: ADR <number> — 「<Words line>」`; the
  Captain may reopen it.
- **L3, decide by record:** not built. A class of decisions moves to L3 only by a Captain
  grant recorded as its own ADR, on ledger evidence that his rulings in that area agreed
  with FO and were not later amended. Any reversal returns the area to L0.

Authority, gate approval, merge, outward-facing actions, irreversible changes and money
are never delegated at any level. A delegated decision is recorded as FO's decision with
its basis, never as the Captain's words.

The decision ledger is derived, not stored: `decision_ledger.py` reads the gate records
SD already writes (who, when, decision, reason, grant, briefing question) plus
`Override:` lines and `## Captain amendments`. The learn extension runs `learn` and the
observer when FO archives a task.

## Consequences

This answers ADR 0009's open trigger at task close for adopters that list the learn
extension. L3 needs `Override:` lines to accumulate before any area shows a record; the
ledger's `amended_after` counts amendments dated on or after a ruling, which approximates
a later reversal and can over-count. Reopen if an L2 precedent is reopened by the Captain
twice in one area, or if the ledger cannot separate areas well enough to support an L3
grant.

# 0004. Review rounds stop by rule and added comments are counted against a maximum

Date: 2026-09-30

## Status

Accepted

> Amended by ADR 0010: from round 3 a declined finding becomes its own backlog task, not a `Follow-up:` line in a task's Scope.

## Context

Two delivery PRs in an adopting project each took four rounds of an external
reviewer; in one the only P1 came in round one, and the Captain ruled the stop ad hoc;
a two-line P1 repair took about 1h40 from the validation approval to its report (dispatch time not recorded) while
another task's worker held the same stage (the state history is consistent with
`concurrency: 1` being read as a hard cap; the cause is not proven); candidates reached validation at 12.6, 7.5 and 6.4
percent added-comment ratio against a 5 percent target and each needed a trim round, and a
comment cited its task's own numbering. Read 2026-09-30 in the task's ideation,
from the adopter's task files and issues #521, #522 and #525. Spacedock 0.27.2
reads `concurrency` only for `status --next`; a feedback-reflow dispatch built
while another entity held the only slot. The Captain's baseline for added comments
is 3 percent, his target 5 percent.

## Decision

**Words:** Captain, all 2026-09-30, in order (ideation gate `review-cadence`, then its validation gate):

- 「套件本身不設預設值 => 為何不要預設就是「基準 3%、目標 5%」？你有想到其他案例是要極端少註解或是明顯拉大閥門數量的嗎？」
- 「此外審查輪數目前應該沒有考慮搭配使用 roborev 的狀況對嗎？它應該也會有一樣的問題，每次審查都有機會找到狀況，要一併考慮，還是等整合用了遇到再說？」
- 「專案可以自己改，具體是怎麼改？改 adoptor 的 readme.md 嗎？」
- 「核准」, approving the design with two amendments: the package default is 5 percent, overridable by `comment-ratio-max:` or `--max`; the round rule (N = 2) applies to any external reviewer.
- 「退回補」 at the validation gate: four repairs, and the constructed false-positive classes of the citation scan declined as a known limit.

**Options considered:**
- rounds 1 and 2 as today; from round 3 only a Material finding or a reviewer P1 starts a repair cycle and the rest become recorded follow-ups (chosen, N = 2)
- no rule, the Captain rules each PR — rejected: it cost repair cycles on two PRs
- cap at 3 rounds like `kc-pr-flow` self-review — rejected: that caps the author's own review, not an external reviewer's findings
- a repair lane keyed on the repair's size — rejected: size is unknown before dispatch; ownership of a worktree and an authorized assignment are known
- ship no comment-ratio default and let each adopter declare it — rejected by the Captain's amendment
- a five-percent default with an adopter key and a `--max` override (chosen)

**Recommended:** not recorded

A delivery PR's review rounds are counted by the first officer. A finding assessed
Material, or labelled P1 by the external reviewer, blocks in every round; a reviewer P1
is fixed and revalidated or waived by the Captain with the reason recorded. From the
third round a finding that is neither starts no repair cycle and becomes a follow-up in
the committed gate summary and a `Follow-up:` line in a task's Scope. A feedback-reflow
repair and an authorized first-officer fix are dispatched at once in the entity's own
worktree, and the validation recheck of either is dispatched after the repair or fix
has completed and committed its candidate; none waits for another entity's worker,
and `concurrency` limits only what `status --next`
proposes (Spacedock 0.27.2; `scripts/test_sd_dispatch.py` builds a reflow dispatch while another entity holds the slot). `comment_ratio.py` exits 1 when added comments exceed the maximum (default 5
percent, `comment-ratio-max:` in the workflow README, `--max` for one run) with at least
20 code lines added, and when an added comment cites task numbering, review provenance,
a PR or issue number or a `file:line`, unless it names an ADR.

## Consequences

A real defect a reviewer labels below P1 and the first officer does not assess Material
is deferred to a follow-up from round 3. The round count, the lane and the follow-up
recording are prose the first officer applies; nothing mechanical enforces them, and
only an adopter's next delivery PR shows whether they hold. The citation scan finds its
named classes only, and it also flags text that only looks like a citation: a `#333`
colour, `step #1`, a URL fragment, an asyncio "Task 3", "a code review of the parser",
"the Codex CLI". Measured on the last 150 commits of origin/main: 38 hits, 1 false
positive. The Captain declined a fix for these classes as a known limit. The

# 0021. A prod task's validation runs one security review that reaches past the diff and the merge-ask check enforces

Date: 2026-10-17

## Status

Accepted

## Context

Relay PR #347 exposed existing comment and session write paths that had no total cap, and that code was outside the PR's diff. On that PR at its reviewed head, `kc-pr-flow:tob-security-reviewer` at `security_tier: full` under its own contract named the prompt injection and never the unbounded writes, on Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 alike (0 of 6 runs). The same agent with one added paragraph (the Reach brief, now in `skills/validation/profiles/prod.md`) named them in 4 of 4 runs (Sonnet twice, Opus once, Fable once) and returned `findings: []` on a Python check script with no public surface. No run of 14 was a refusal. Cost per review on Sonnet, relay size: 0.86 to 0.91 USD assumed (4.07 to 4.33 ceiling); Opus about 2.2 and Fable about 12.3 for the same paragraph. "Assumed" prices cache writes at 1.25x and reads at 0.1x the input price, and output tokens are estimated; neither is verified. ADR 0019 left the validation-gate review and the default model to this task.

## Decision

**Words:** 「那就照建議」 — Captain, 2026-10-17, chat, approving the six batch-2 ideation gates, each of which stated its recommendations (this task's D1 to D4)

**Options considered:**
- D1 model and effort: `model: sonnet` for validation and ideation, one agent definition (chosen); Opus or Fable by public surface, or a second definition by complexity — not chosen: the model was not the lever in 14 runs and effort was never varied
- D2 refusal: hold, no rerun and no model switch (chosen); rerun on Opus — not chosen: never exercised, and the worker would swap the model that refused
- D3 enforcement: `delivery_gate.py check` at the merge ask plus the command in the worker's acceptance script, no FO word changed (chosen); an FO step in `### validation` — not chosen: about 25 words in a file 16 words under budget
- D4 rerun: a new review for every new candidate head (chosen); a rule keyed to "touches a public surface" — not chosen: it asks the worker to judge exposure, the step that failed on #347

**Recommended:** the first option of each of D1 to D4, as the Captain accepted.

A prod task's validation worker dispatches the reviewer once with the Reach brief, saves the report as `security/validation-<N>.yaml`, writes `Security review (validation): <path> at <head>` and one `Security finding (validation <N>) <n>:` line per finding (`Material`, `declined` on MEDIUM or LOW only, or `Needs decision`). `validation_security.py`, called from `delivery_gate.py check`, refuses a prod task with no review, a `not run` review, a review at any head but the dispatched one the PR head equals, a profile line it cannot read as poc, pilot or prod, a repeated finding line, a report that is not a `tob_security_review` report, a finding with no line, a declined HIGH or CRITICAL, or an open Material finding. A reply with no report is saved, recorded as `not run: reviewer returned no report (<model>)`, and holds the stage, at ideation and at validation.

## Consequences

FO reads 10 more words at the merge ask of a prod task and none elsewhere; each prod review costs the amounts above, again for each new candidate head. The check proves a report with this shape exists at a dispatched head and every finding has a disposition; it cannot tell a real zero-finding report from a fabricated one, or which brief produced it. A worker that skips the review meets the hold at the merge ask, not at the validation gate. The Reach brief is fitted to one miss on one PR from one repository; Opus and Fable are n=1 each. An adopter without kc-pr-flow, or a Codex-hosted worker that cannot dispatch the Claude agent, holds every prod validation. Reopen if a refusal occurs, if a stronger model finds a class Sonnet misses under the same brief, or if the brief misses a write class on another repository.

# Maintain flow

Invocation: `kc-dev-flow-2:maintain-flow`

Read the [framework](../../README.md) and the affected skill's routing table.
Put cross-stage profile principles in their one shared reference, stage-common
practices in principles.md, and differences in that stage's profiles directory.
Preserve exact variant namespaces and the POC ideation skip; avoid copying a
shared rule into each profile or adding unused automation scaffolding.

Every adopter copies `references/sd/workflow.md` as its workflow README, and the
implementation and validation stages inline its `context-sections` into each
dispatch, so its text costs every FO and worker. For each rule added to it,
state in the change: the incident it answers; whether a package script, test or
SD command already enforces it, in which case write one sentence naming that
enforcer instead of restating it; and which existing sentence it replaces, or
that it replaces none. Before adding, look for a sentence to shorten or remove.
Report the file's word count before and after, and the words each worker stage
inlines. `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/lint-skills.py` refuses a file whose count differs from its word budget and a passage of
12 or more words that another package file repeats; a raise of the budget needs a Captain ruling
in the budget steps, a cut lowers it in the same change, and listing an overlap says why.

Run `python3 kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/lint-skills.py` from the repository root. Before each push
of a package change, run `python3 kc-dev-flow-2/extensions/roborev/roborev_gate.py --repo
<worktree> --base <merge base>` and fix what it reports inside the change: a maintainer
change is not dispatched through FO, so no implementation stage runs it.
When changing lint behavior, run `python3 kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/test_lint_skills.py`
and add a mutation only for a material failure the check is meant to catch.
Use an available Agent Skills specification validator for broader authoring
format checks; the bundled CLI reuses the repository's basic frontmatter check
and validates declared routing structure and package script paths, not the full
standard or agent behavior.

An optional tool joins as an extension: a folder `kc-dev-flow-2/extensions/<name>/` holding
its scripts, their tests and an `EXTENSION.md` in the shape of the existing ones. The workflow
mentions extensions only in its `## Extensions` section and the README's `extensions:` list,
so a repository that lists none is unchanged.

A script that newly needs a line or step only FO writes must also print it from a script the
previous release's README already has FO run at that moment, shown by running the new scripts over
the previous release's record shape; no check enforces this.

## Behaviour replay

A change that claims a worker will act differently is shown before release, because
wording tests prove only that the text is there. Pick a closed adopter task whose record
holds the old behaviour, and build its dispatch twice with
`python3 kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/replay_dispatch.py build`: once at the last release tag
and once at the change, from the same state and code commits, with a checklist that
names no rule under test. Run each as a fresh worker on the same model, once on the
release and at least twice on the change; `--inject` adds the FO record a rule
depends on, such as a decline. The helper adds the line naming `main` as the completion
recipient to the scope notes; `--no-completion-line` builds the arm without it. Report a table of runs by outcome, then run
`python3 kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/replay_dispatch.py cleanup`. A rule only FO acts on cannot be replayed: a fresh FO
answers scenario questions from the README alone, including one where the rule must not
apply. A replay that contradicts the claim stops the change; after two rewordings that
still fail, take a structural option to the Captain instead of a third.

## Observe adopters

FO grading its own work misses what an outside reader finds, so after each release the
maintainer reads the first task each adopter archives on it. Where the adopter lists
`learn`, that task's `observer.md` is the report; otherwise dispatch
`kc-dev-flow-2:observer` with that adopter's state checkout, the slug and its README.
Before counting a rule as broken twice, read the other tasks' `observer.md` files too;
`python3 kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/decision_ledger.py <state> --summary` adds the counts of
rulings, delegated decisions, overrides and later amendments per area. Find every
reported quote in git before acting on it and retract one that is not there. Send each
confirmed finding to the FO that owns the task, with the quote and the ruling it needs,
and record the ruling it gets. A rule broken in two tasks becomes a package change: a
script check with a mutation test when the rule is objective, otherwise a rewording
shown by Behaviour replay. Read the adopters' workflow sync PRs too: their external
review reads the package text as a reviewer outside the package does.

Report the exact changed files, static results, replay table and untested behavioral claims.
Do not infer permission to register/install the bundle, execute SD stages,
install hooks, launch experiments, post externally or commit from a lint pass.

## Context

A prod-profile task on a sibling repository passed ideation, implementation and validation with no security question. - an opt-in `security` extension that FO reads and dispatches at two gates (the first design; withdrawn by amendment 2, wrong carrier for "always": it is opt-in and read by FO)
- a new security reviewer agent in this package — not chosen: `kc-pr-flow:tob-security-reviewer` exists and fits
- D1 focus file: the one path `.claude/agents/security-reviewer.md` (chosen); a README key naming the path — not chosen, one more adopter setting
- D3 model: the agent's declared Sonnet until the validation-gate task's three-model measurement reports (chosen); a stronger model now — not measured

# 0024. An FO rule whose only witness is the Captain's chat or a shell run is listed as not judged

Date: 2026-10-19

## Status

Accepted

## Context

The observer reports on six batch-2 tasks marked 18 rows `can't tell`, naming 17 FO rules in 40 rule-report pairs. Each row was judged by one question: who or what can see the evidence, and does anyone need it later. 10 pairs are readable from state (`design_surfaces.py check` replayed at the task-file sha a briefing binds; `merge/ask-<N>.json`, written by `delivery_gate.py check` since 0.25.0). 4 are held by FO alone and no one else sees them (the sufficiency and necessity confirmation before a merge ask). 16 are witnessed only by the Captain's chat or by a shell run that leaves no record. 10 are not chat-only and stay as they are or go to `fo-write-checks` and `captain-question-load`. Replaying `design_surfaces.py check` over history exits 1 in 11 of 82 runs for a section the task's gate did not yet need, which is ADR 0017's reason a law over history is red by age; ADR 0014 already accepts that `workflow_checkout.py` is prose-enforced.

## Decision

**Words:** 「照建議」 — Captain, 2026-10-19, chat, approving the four batch-3 ideation gates presented together. This task's gate question read: "Approving accepts D1 (the observer stops judging the rules only chat can show: the acceptance steps in full, the package and checkout runs, answering a Captain question, the --names run, the four-field assessment, while the rest are read from state or recorded), D2 (Sufficiency: and Necessity: clauses in the delivery gate text, held by delivery_gate.py), D3 (the acceptance steps shown in full stay chat-only), and FO's implementation order below."

**Options considered:**
- D1 list the chat-only rules in the observer skill as not judged, replay or read the ones state holds, and lint each listed phrase against `references/sd/workflow.md` (chosen); keep reporting all of them `can't tell` — not chosen, it names rules the observer can never see
- D2 `delivery_gate.py` holds a merge ask whose text has no `Sufficiency:` or `Necessity:` clause and saves both in `ask-<N>.json` (chosen); list the confirmation as not judged — not chosen, no one but FO sees it
- D3 the acceptance steps in full stay chat-only (chosen); save the observed output and pass it to `gate prepare --reference` — not chosen, it needs a README sentence and a budget raise under ADR 0020

**Recommended:** D1, D2 and D3 as chosen, as the task design stated and the Captain accepted.

An FO rule whose only witness is the Captain's chat, or a shell run that leaves no record, is listed in the observer skill as not judged. It gets a record only when a later reader needs one. `lint-skills.py` fails when a listed phrase is not in `references/sd/workflow.md`, so a reworded rule cannot leave the list unnoticed.

## Consequences

The observer stops reporting 16 of the 40 pairs and reads 10 more from state; a first merge ask without both clauses holds once and the hold line names what to add, and an adopter meets that hold at its first ask after a plugin update. `delivery_gate.py` checks that a clause is present, not that it is true, so `Necessity: yes` passes. Worse: an FO that shortens the acceptance steps or skips `workflow_checkout.py` leaves nothing the observer can show, so only the Captain's attention and the script's own hold catch it. Reopen if an observer report or the Captain finds a listed rule broken with nothing in state or chat to show it, if a gate is found presented where `design_surfaces.py check` exits 1 at its bound sha, or if Spacedock gains a pre-dispatch hook (ADR 0014).

  commit that added the task file and `TO` is the state checkout's `HEAD`.

## Read

1. `git -C STATE log --format='%h %ad %s' --date=iso FROM..TO -- <task file> <task dir>`
   and the diff over the same range. Read the task at `TO` only around changed hunks. For an
   archived task give git both path pairs, `<TASK>.md <TASK>` and `_archive/<TASK>.md
   _archive/<TASK>`, and take `FROM` from the commit that added `<TASK>.md`; the archive
   commit alone leaves a window of one commit.
2. `python3 <package>/scripts/decision_ledger.py STATE`, keeping the rows for `TASK`:
   each gate ruling with its question, who recorded it, its grant and any `Override:`.
3. From RULES collect every sentence whose subject is FO ("FO records", "FO appends",
   "FO declines", "FO reserves", "FO names", "FO counts", "FO applies") and that applied
   in this window. Quote each with its section heading.

Check at least: a Captain ruling quotes his words and answers a question put before it;
an approval read as accepting a recommendation has that sentence in its question; a
decision by `agent:first-officer` carries the grant it relies on; an `Override:` line
exists where his choice differs from the stated recommendation; a `Precedent:` names an
ADR and quotes its Words line, or its decision sentence when marked `(no Words line)`,
and is not one of the always-asked kinds; amendments and
`Asked:` lines follow `## Captain amendments`; declines follow step 5 of review findings.
Where RULES list `peers` under `extensions:`, also check that no Captain ruling in the task
quotes a peer's words, or a peer's report of the Captain, in place of his own; a ruling he
made in his own words after reading peer data is his. An exchange the file does not record
is outside what state shows.

Replay the design check. For each backlog and ideation briefing, take the sha in its artifact `uri`
(`git-root://state/<sha>/<TASK>.md`), extract `<TASK>.md` and, when it exists at that sha, `<TASK>/` with
`git archive` into a new empty temporary directory, and run
`python3 <package>/scripts/design_surfaces.py check [--seed, for backlog] <that copy of <TASK>.md>`.
Report "FO runs `python3 <package>/scripts/design_surfaces.py check`" as `ok` on exit 0, and as `violation` quoting its first line on exit 1.

Where `<TASK>/merge/ask-<N>.json` files exist, each is a passing run of `python3 <package>/scripts/delivery_gate.py check`.
FO runs it again after the Captain approves, just before merging, so the highest N usually postdates the briefing.
Read the highest-numbered file whose `head` starts with the head the question names and whose `time` is not after the commit
that added that ask's briefing. Report "FO runs `python3 <package>/scripts/delivery_gate.py check` before the merge ask" as `ok`,
quoting that file's `time` and `head`. When files for that head exist but every one is later than that commit, report `can't tell`
quoting the earliest `time` and the commit time: the file cannot show whether FO ran the check before presenting. When no file
exists the task may predate the record, so report `can't tell`. Report "FO confirms both goal sufficiency and minimal necessity"
from the same file: `ok` quoting `sufficiency` and `necessity`; `can't tell` when it holds neither key, which predates that check.

Do not report these rules. Their only witness is the Captain's chat or a shell run that leaves no record, so
the report would only say `can't tell`:

<!-- chat-only-rules -->
- presents every step in full beside its observed output
- FO answers a question the Captain asks at a gate
- python3 <package>/scripts/package_version.py
- python3 <package>/scripts/workflow_checkout.py
- python3 <package>/scripts/dispatch_records.py --names
- assess the four evidence fields above
<!-- /chat-only-rules -->

A rule outside this list that you cannot judge stays `can't tell`.

For a task whose `Surfaces:` include `db`, whose ideation ran on a stronger model, or
whose validation was sent back twice, report whether a `Reviewer:` line exists. That
line is a record, not a requirement: report it as `observed`, never as a violation.
Separately, run `python3 <package>/scripts/role_triggers.py STATE TASK --rev TO` and report each
`next:` line it prints as `violation`, quoting that line.

## Prove each finding

Before reporting a finding, find its evidence quote with `git -C STATE show TO:<path>`,
`git grep` or the ledger output, and drop it if the quote is not there. A rule that did
not apply in the window is not listed. Decide the verdict word last, from the evidence
you wrote.

## Return (under 500 words)

One line per finding:
`<violation|ok|can't tell|observed> | rule: "<quoted rule>" (<section>) | evidence: "<quoted line or 'absent'>" (<commit>)`

`can't tell` names the evidence that is outside state (chat, a PR, a database).
Then `Coverage:` what you read fully, what you sampled, and each rule you could not
evaluate.

## Boundaries

Read-only: no edit, commit, push, comment or message. Do not judge product content,
design quality or worker reports, and do not propose a repair. The caller passes the
report on unedited; whoever owns the task answers it.

1. Q: Before which action must a needed consultation finish, and does an unanswered consultation stop that action?
   Story: special-role-calls-fire-when-needed
   Grounds: `pr_watch.tasks()` emits consultation instructions during startup or idle in `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/pr_watch.py`; `kc-dev-flow-2/README.md` says neither role is “a routine gate.”
   Why it matters: A reminder that arrives after implementation or merge would not prevent the failures described.

2. Q: What evidence should establish that a design reverses an earlier Captain ruling when neither `Supersedes:` nor `Design:` names the replacement?
   Story: special-role-calls-fire-when-needed
   Grounds: The story names “a design or amendment reversing an earlier Captain ruling”; `events()` in `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/role_triggers.py` recognizes only particular amendment fields.
   Why it matters: Detecting an unrecorded reversal requires a comparison against prior decisions, beyond recognizing new text.

3. Q: What distinguishes repeated findings that require consultation from unrelated findings that happen to concern the same file?
   Story: special-role-calls-fire-when-needed
   Grounds: The story identifies “two or more review rounds finding new gaps in one file or sentence”; `kc-dev-flow-2/skills/chief-engineer/SKILL.md` names work “repeatedly circling.”
   Why it matters: File overlap alone could summon advisers for ordinary review while missing one underlying problem spread across files.

4. Q: When repeated repairs also expose a contested technical claim, should both roles be called or should one consultation determine whether the other is needed?
   Story: special-role-calls-fire-when-needed
   Grounds: `kc-dev-flow-2/skills/chief-engineer/SKILL.md` covers circling work, while `kc-dev-flow-2/skills/engineering-reviewer/SKILL.md` covers conflicting evidence on material claims.
   Why it matters: Both triggers can apply to the same incident, changing dispatch order, delay and cost.

5. Q: Which consultation obligations may the First Officer waive without a Captain decision?
   Story: special-role-calls-fire-when-needed
   Grounds: `owed_line()` offers “if you will not” record a waiver, and `cleared()` accepts any nonblank reason in `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/role_triggers.py`.
   Why it matters: Unrestricted waivers could preserve the reported absence of calls while making every check pass.

6. Q: What evidence must exist before a consultation counts as completed rather than merely requested?
   Story: special-role-calls-fire-when-needed
   Grounds: `cleared()` in `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/role_triggers.py` accepts a `Reviewer:` line containing an agent, model, date and question without reading a response.
   Why it matters: Recording an intended call currently satisfies the same check as receiving usable advice.

7. Q: Which changes to the reviewed artifact or decision invalidate an earlier consultation?
   Story: special-role-calls-fire-when-needed
   Grounds: The engineering-reviewer report includes an exact `revision` in `kc-dev-flow-2/skills/engineering-reviewer/SKILL.md`, but `cleared()` checks only the amendment token and calendar date.
   Why it matters: Advice about an earlier version could clear an obligation after the relevant claim has changed.

8. Q: What new evidence should require another chief-engineer consultation after an earlier call has been satisfied?
   Story: special-role-calls-fire-when-needed
   Grounds: `check()` in `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/role_triggers.py` collapses every cycle numbered three or higher into one obligation cleared by `Cycle 3`.
   Why it matters: One early call currently suppresses further calls even if repairs continue or a different blocker emerges.

9. Q: How should a resumed or concurrent First Officer distinguish an unanswered consultation already running from one that still needs dispatch?
   Story: special-role-calls-fire-when-needed
   Grounds: `pr_watch.tasks()` repeats owed instructions, while `cleared()` in `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/role_triggers.py` recognizes completed-call text or waivers but no pending state.
   Why it matters: Recovery can otherwise duplicate expensive calls or treat a lost call as completed.

10. Q: When stage reports, feedback-cycle entries and external-review verdicts describe the same work, what constitutes one consultation-triggering round?
    Story: special-role-calls-fire-when-needed
    Grounds: The story contrasts `Stage Report: ... (cycle N)` with `- Cycle N`; `kc-dev-flow-2/references/sd/workflow.md` separately defines a round as an external reviewer’s verdict.
    Why it matters: Combining these sources without deciding their relationship could double-count repairs or miss repeated reviews.

11. Q: Should an unrecognized or missing event format mean no consultation is needed, or that the need cannot be determined?
    Story: special-role-calls-fire-when-needed
    Grounds: `events()` and `check()` in `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/role_triggers.py` return success with zero recognized events; the story reports this outcome for two repositories.
    Why it matters: Successful parsing and absence of evidence currently produce the same reassuring result.

12. Q: Must existing calls written as “third repair cycle” or under another heading satisfy their obligations without rewriting historical records?
    Story: special-role-calls-fire-when-needed
    Grounds: The story reports genuine calls rejected for wording or placement; `test_each_near_miss_leaves_the_event_owed()` and `test_only_the_fo_alignment_section_can_clear_an_event()` in `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/test_role_triggers.py` enforce those restrictions.
    Why it matters: Compatibility determines whether adoption recognizes earlier work or creates duplicate consultation requests.

13. Q: How should a newly recognized consultation obligation be handled when the relevant action has already merged or the task is archived?
    Story: special-role-calls-fire-when-needed
    Grounds: The story includes a consultation “waived after the merge”; `test_an_archived_task_owing_a_role_call_prints_nothing()` in `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/test_pr_watch.py` explicitly excludes archived work.
    Why it matters: Retrospective accounting and advice that can still change an outcome require different behavior.

14. Q: Which new triggers override the proof-of-concept profile’s default of no consultation?
    Story: special-role-calls-fire-when-needed
    Grounds: `kc-dev-flow-2/README.md` says “POC defaults to no consultation,” while `check()` in `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/role_triggers.py` does not inspect the profile.
    Why it matters: Applying every trigger uniformly could add obligations to a deliberately lighter route.

15. Q: What ensures a freshly dispatched adviser receives the adopter’s secret-access restrictions before its first tool call?
    Story: special-role-calls-fire-when-needed
    Grounds: `docs/adr/0003-secret-reads-are-enforced-by-the-adopter.md` records two secret leaks despite written bans; the role wrappers in `kc-dev-flow-2/agents/` invoke their skills without naming the workflow’s `Dispatch facts`.
    Why it matters: More automatic consultations create more execution contexts that need the existing permission boundary.

16. Q: What may continue when a required role cannot run on its declared model and reasoning level?
    Story: special-role-calls-fire-when-needed
    Grounds: `kc-dev-flow-2/references/sd/workflow.md` requires the roles’ declared settings, “never a cheaper one”; `owed_line()` in `kc-dev-flow-2/scripts/role_triggers.py` offers dispatch or waiver without distinguishing unavailability.
    Why it matters: Runtime failure needs a defined outcome without silently weakening the role or blocking unrelated work.

17. Q: What consultation spending or elapsed-time limit should return the decision to the Captain?
    Story: special-role-calls-fire-when-needed
    Grounds: Both role agents declare `model: opus` and `reasoning: xhigh`; `kc-dev-flow-2/references/sd/workflow.md` requires preserving the approved budget and stop condition.
    Why it matters: Broader triggers can consume the task’s budget even when each individual call is justified.

18. Q: Must the new behavior work for adopters using the previous workflow instructions, or is an approved workflow update required before it applies?
    Story: special-role-calls-fire-when-needed
    Grounds: The story names every adopting First Officer as a consumer; `kc-dev-flow-2/skills/maintain-flow/SKILL.md` requires new First Officer steps to surface through scripts the previous release already invokes.
    Why it matters: Publishing changed instructions does not establish that existing sessions will encounter or follow them.

19. Q: Which judgment-based missed calls should become observer violations rather than observations?
    Story: special-role-calls-fire-when-needed
    Grounds: `kc-dev-flow-2/skills/observer/SKILL.md` treats missing `Reviewer:` lines for stronger-model ideation or twice-rejected validation as “observed,” but treats script-reported obligations as “violation.”
    Why it matters: The story’s broader meaning of “needed” must align with how compliance is assessed.

20. Q: Which reported incidents and ordinary-work counterexamples must a fresh First Officer handle correctly before this story is accepted?
    Story: special-role-calls-fire-when-needed
    Grounds: The story cites reports in `fo-batch-sittings/dogfood/`, which is absent from this snapshot; `kc-dev-flow-2/skills/maintain-flow/SKILL.md` requires First Officer scenarios including one where the rule must not apply.
    Why it matters: Parser tests cannot demonstrate that appropriate calls actually happen, and the cited incidents need primary evidence before becoming acceptance cases.
